fields.description: The idempotency key for one @triton turn, derived from the triggering mention rather than generated. Unique, so a redelivered interaction event or a double-tapped mention produces one turn and not two answers - and so the whole cost of a turn is one row rather than a set nobody can join.
fields.label: Request ID

fields.description: Where the turn got to. `Refused` is distinct from `Failed` on purpose: refused means the system declined (no ERPNext link, retrieval paused, not whitelisted), failed means it tried and broke, and conflating them makes a rollout problem look like an outage.
fields.label: Status
fields.options:
Received
Retrieving
Generating
Answered
Failed
Refused

fields.description: Which client the mention came from. Recorded for observability ONLY - the handler itself cannot see this field, because identical behaviour from either origin is guaranteed by the handler having no origin to branch on rather than by a reviewer checking that it does not.
fields.label: Origin

fields.description: The human who typed the mention. Every tool call and every chat read in this turn ran as this person - never as a service account, and never as the bot that posts the answer. Those are two different identities and merging them is how a superuser service account gets built.
fields.label: Asked By

fields.description: The message Triton posted. In the same room and the same thread as the mention, always - never a room derived from model output.
fields.label: Answer Message

fields.description: Why the turn failed or was refused, scrubbed. Never a message body and never a bearer token.
fields.label: Error

fields.description: Retrieved chat context only, excluding the system prompt and tool definitions - the number the ceiling actually governs. Logged on EVERY turn, because the ceiling was chosen deliberately rather than derived from a model limit, and the only honest way to retune it is two weeks of this column.
fields.label: Context Tokens

fields.description: Tokens served from the model's context cache, as reported upstream. This is the column that says whether prompt-cache ordering is actually paying: a stable prefix that never engages the cache costs the full discount silently, with no error and no log line anywhere.
fields.label: Cached Content Tokens

fields.description: Set when the degradation ladder reached a rung that removes information the user would expect to be there. When this is set, Triton is instructed to SAY its view was cut - a model that silently answers from a truncated view produces a confident wrong answer and the user gets no signal at all.
fields.label: Context Truncated

fields.description: How far down the fixed ladder assembly had to go: 0 for no degradation, then 1..5. Stored as a number rather than a flag so the common case can be told from the extreme one - rung 1 drops the least useful chunks, rung 5 is a hard floor of the last twenty messages.
fields.label: Degradation Rung

fields.description: Candidate chunks after the permission filter and before ranking. The vector backend's revisit triggers are written against THIS number rather than the corpus size, because the filter runs first: past the configured threshold the in-process cosine stops being the right implementation and the adapter swap becomes a scheduled task rather than a debate.
fields.label: Chunks Considered

fields.description: Citations the model emitted that resolved to nothing in the manifest. Dropped silently in the rendered answer - a broken citation must not become a broken page - but counted here, because a miss rate above a couple of percent is a PROMPT regression signal rather than a UI bug.
fields.label: Citation Miss Count

fields.description:
The citation manifest for this answer, as JSON, in the shape public/js/chat/citations.js already reads: k, type, label, url, room, message. It lives here rather than on Chat Message because the hot table must not grow a column for one sender's messages - and because a manifest is metadata about a turn, which is what this table is.

Deliberately carries NO snippet. The client would render one in a tooltip, and a snippet is message text; storing it here would put conversation into the one chat table that is content-free by construction. The label says who and which room, and clicking is what shows the message - under the full permission check, through the deep link.
fields.label: Citations (JSON)

fields.description: Time inside the gate: derive the room set, filter, rank, assemble. The revisit trigger is a p95 over this column.
fields.label: Retrieval (ms)

fields.description: How long the turn sat between being acknowledged and being picked up by a worker. The interaction webhook has a hard 30-second deadline, so the model turn can never answer inline - it acknowledges, enqueues, and posts asynchronously. This column is what says whether that queue is healthy, and a growing value is the first symptom of a backed-up worker.
fields.label: Queue (ms)
